name: False Dichotomy
shortDef: Presenting two options as the only ones when others exist.
definition: Framing a decision as either/or, so that rejecting one option seems to force the other, when reasonable alternatives, combinations or in-between paths have been left out.
howToSpot: Can you name a realistic third option the speaker skipped?
Does rejecting one choice really force you into the other?
Ask whether both options could be combined, delayed or done partly.
classicExample: Either we ban phones in class completely, or we accept that students will never pay attention again.
legitimateVersion: It's fair when the two options truly exhaust the possibilities, like a motion that either passes or fails, or when the other options have already been ruled out with stated reasons.

contrast.fal_middle_ground: A false dichotomy hides the other options; middle ground assumes the option between two extremes must be the right one.
contrast.fal_loaded_question: A false dichotomy offers too few choices; a loaded question slips an unproven assumption into the question itself.
